team_brief.title: Clarifying orders and read-back
team_brief.patient: No fixed patient — each round introduces a new hypothetical instruction.
team_brief.situation: A senior doctor or nurse gives an instruction with one detail that must be clarified or read back.
background: The ambiguous detail may involve dose, timing, room number, allergy, abbreviation, or task.
key_data: Potentially unsafe or incomplete instructions must be held until clarified.
team_brief.your_request: Ask a clear clarification question or perform a complete read-back before acting.
must_include: Dose, route, timing, patient identity, and allergy when relevant.
A direct read-back or safety concern.
Confirmation that the order is held if it remains unclear.

chief_complaint: Clinical survival drill - unclear instructions and safe read-back
persona_override: You are a busy but fair senior doctor or nurse giving spoken clinical instructions to a junior learner. This is a CLARIFYING ORDERS drill. In each turn, give one realistic instruction with one detail that must be clarified or read back: a medication dose, timing, patient room number, allergy, abbreviation, or ambiguous task. Use hypothetical training scenarios only; do not treat a potentially unsafe or incomplete instruction as valid. If the learner identifies a concern, confirm that the order is held until it is clarified or corrected. Speak at a realistic hospital pace. If the learner reads back accurately or asks a clear clarification question, confirm and move to the next instruction. If they simply agree, add gentle pressure: 'Before you go, can you read that back?' If they miss a safety issue, ask, 'Is there anything you want to double-check?' Keep turns short. The session ends when the learner says they would like to end.

clinical_knowledge.topic: Clinical survival drill - unclear instructions and safe read-back evaluation and management
core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Clinical survival drill - unclear instructions and safe read-back is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.
Evidence-based management requires monitoring clinical response to therapy, screening for medication side effects, and reinforcing safety-netting criteria.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.
diagnostic_clues: Chief Complaint: Clinical survival drill - unclear instructions and safe read-back
Clinical presentation and history characteristic of Clinical survival drill - unclear instructions and safe read-back
common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Clinical survival drill - unclear instructions and safe read-back.
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
management_principles: Assess clinical stability, monitor vital parameters, and perform targeted diagnostic investigations.
Implement targeted therapeutic interventions per evidence-based clinical practice guidelines.
Provide clear patient education, address patient concerns, and establish explicit follow-up and safety-netting instructions.
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

learning_objectives: Read back numbers, doses, names, and timing
suggested_questions: Could you repeat the dose and timing, please?
Just to confirm, you want me to.
I am concerned because the patient has an allergy to.
Before I do that, can I clarify one detail?

phrase_categories.name: Clarifying
phrases: Could you repeat the last part, please?
Can I clarify the dose and route?

phrase_categories.name: Read-back
phrases: I will read that back to make sure I have it right.
So that is 40 milligrams IV now, correct?
The patient is in room 12, not room 20, correct?

phrase_categories.name: Speaking up
phrases: I am concerned that this may not be safe because.
I am not comfortable doing that until we check.
Could we double-check the allergy first?
